clues: This is the biggest city in Brazil. It is the chief town of its state, and the most full of folk in the south half of the world.
Summer here is hot and rainy, but winter brings a twist. Cold air from the far south drifts in at times, and grey clouds hang over town.
Priests of the Jesuit order set up this city in 1554. Few towns in the New World have been lived in without a break since such old days.
This city is a great mix of folk from all round the world. It holds the largest groups of Arab, Italian, and Japanese folk who live far from their old homes.
Its famed Ibirapuera Park is one of the best loved sights here. It sits with museums and great halls on the list of the city's top places to see.
